segments.text: Let us solve this equation.
Two x, plus three, equals eleven.
Two x means two copies of an unknown number.
Plus three adds three units. The total is eleven.
Equality means both sides have the same value. Picture a balanced scale.
Here are two unknown bags and three units on the left. Eleven units on the right.
To isolate the bags, subtract three from both sides. Write minus three under each side.
These matching operations preserve equality.
Plus three and minus three cancel to zero.
Select three units on each side.
Remove those three units from both sides. The balance stays equal.
Write the next line: two x equals eight.
Now divide both sides by two. Draw a fraction bar under each side.
Write two below each bar. Both sides are divided by the same number.
Split the eight remaining units into two equal groups.
Each group contains four units. So x equals four.
Check in the original equation. Replace x with four.
Two times four is eight. Add three.
Eight plus three is eleven. Both sides match.
Your turn. Solve three x plus two equals fourteen.
